result.rationale: In sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts). The zohocrm CalendarService diff then assigns that Response to zohoCrmTokenInfo and immediately reads zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error — Responses have no .data property, so this throws a TypeError whenever credential sharing is enabled with a sync endpoint, breaking Zoho CRM token refresh. The same missing parsing issue exists for lark/zoho-bigin (they pass the Response to handlers expecting fetch Response, which is fine) but for axios-based zoho code the .data access breaks. Veri

judged_text: In sync mode zohoCrmTokenInfo is a fetch Response, so zohoCrmTokenInfo.data is undefined and the unchanged check !zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error throws TypeError. Zoho CRM token refresh under credential sharing always fails, so synced credentials cannot refresh and calendar operations fail once the initial token expires.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`, token refresh now calls `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then immediately dereferences `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` (e.g. `if (!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error) { ... }`). But `refreshOAuthTokens` (new file `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`) returns a `fetch(...)` `Response` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is truthy. A `Response` object does not have a `.data` property, so in sync mode `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` is `undefined` and `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` will throw a `TypeError`. This is directly induced by the diff.
